title: Andrew Johnson — The Life, The Rise, And The Legacy #Shorts
description:
Somebody like Andrew Johnson should not have made it — that is exactly why the story survives. Andrew Johnson (December 29, 1808 – July 31, 1875) was the 17th president of the United States, serving from 1865 to 1869. The 16th vice president, he assumed the presidency following the assassination of Abraham Lincoln.

Each stage of the life of Andrew Johnson made the next stage possible. In 1835, Johnson made a bid for election to the "floater" (open) seat which Greene County shared with neighboring Washington County in the Tennessee House of Representatives. Trefousse, Johnson "demolished" the opposition in debate and won the election with a near-two-to-one margin.
